summary: Checks whether a value is a non-empty array whose every element is an array.
description:
This is the shape `Range#getValues` returns and `Range#setValues` expects: rows holding cells. `is2DArray` answers
only the shape question — whether the rows all have the same length is
[`isConsistent2DArray`](isConsistent2DArray.md).

An empty array is **not** two-dimensional here: there are no rows to examine, and treating `[]` as a matrix is what
lets an empty result slip through into a `setValues` call that then fails. Nothing else about the elements is
inspected, so a matrix of mixed types passes.
As a TypeScript type predicate it narrows the value to `Array<Array<unknown>>` inside the branch.
returns: `true` if the value is a non-empty array and every element of it is an array; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What counts as two-dimensional
examples.body:
```javascript
is2DArray([[1, 2], [3]]); // => true — ragged, but still 2D
is2DArray([[1], 2]); // => false — one element is not an array
is2DArray([]); // => false — no rows
is2DArray("abc"); // => false
```

examples.title: Guarding a value that may be a matrix
examples.body:
<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="is2DArray.ts" include-symbol="countCells"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function countCells(value) {
  if (!is2DArray(value)) {
    return 0;
  }
  return value.reduce((total, row) => total + row.length, 0);
}
</code-block>
</tab>
</tabs>
